blocks.content:
Solved Example:

Statements:

All soldiers are disciplined.

Some disciplined are officers.



Conclusion:

Some soldiers are officers.

Logic:

Not necessarily true (no direct link)

Answer:

Conclusion does not follow
Check conclusions one by one. Do not assume anything extra.

rows: Directly mentioned or implied in the text
Brought in from outside real-world knowledge
Strictly bounded by the given premises
Must be 100% mathematically or logically sound
Based on real-world probability or general facts

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Evaluate each conclusion independently without letting the validity of one bias another.
Treat all given statements as 100% true, even if they contradict known real-world facts.
Never introduce external facts, general knowledge, or personal assumptions into the reasoning process.
A conclusion is valid only if it logically and directly follows from the explicitly stated premises.
Avoid the trap of choosing a conclusion because it is factually true in real life; it must be true within the context of the statement.
Watch out for definitive words like 'All', 'Always', or 'Never' in conclusions—they are rarely valid unless explicitly backed by the text.
Always verify both conclusions individually before selecting 'Either I or II follows' or 'Neither follows'.
